summary: 48-year-old man 3 weeks after anterior resection with loop ileostomy, output 2.5 L/day, postural hypotension; sodium 126, urine sodium 8, creatinine 142.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Dizzy and thirsty with very watery stoma output
inputs.hpi: Loop ileostomy formed 3 weeks ago at anterior resection for rectal cancer. Stoma output 2.5 litres a day of watery fluid for 5 days; drinking lots of water and tea. Dizzy on standing, thirsty, cramps, passing little urine.

exam.general: Dry mucous membranes, reduced skin turgor. Pulse 108/min lying, BP 102/60 lying falling to 84/50 standing, RR 16, temperature 36.8°C.
exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Healthy ileostomy with high-volume watery effluent; midline wound healed.

comorbidities: Rectal cancer (anterior resection, defunctioning loop ileostomy)
surgicalHistory: Laparoscopic anterior resection with loop ileostomy 3 weeks ago

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Hypovolaemic hyponatraemia with AKI (high-output ileostomy)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Hypovolaemic hyponatraemia (Na 126, urine Na 8) with pre-renal AKI from high-output ileostomy and hypotonic oral intake.

mustInclude.note: Hypovolaemic hyponatraemia: restore volume with isotonic crystalloid.

mustExclude.note: Fluid restriction offered without a volume assessment worsens hypovolaemia and AKI.

guideline.name: European clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia (ESE/ESICM/ERBP)
guideline.section: Severe symptoms (seizure, vomiting, reduced consciousness): 150 mL 3% hypertonic saline over 20 min, repeated (up to twice) checking sodium, target +5 mmol/L; moderately severe symptoms: single 150 mL 3% infusion; limit the rise to 10 mmol/L in the first 24 h and 8 mmol/L in each subsequent 24 h; hypovolaemic hyponatraemia: restore volume with 0.9% saline or balanced crystalloid; SIADH: fluid restriction first line; stop contributing drugs
guideline.citation: Spasovski G, Vanholder R, Allolio B, et al. Clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia. Eur J Endocrinol. 2014;170:G1–47.

guideline.name: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
guideline.section: Detection (creatinine against baseline); urinalysis for all with AKI; ultrasound of the urinary tract within 24 h when obstruction is suspected (immediately if pyonephrosis suspected); stop/withhold nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics) and review metformin; refer to urology immediately for pyonephrosis, obstructed solitary kidney, bilateral upper tract obstruction or complications of obstruction; nephrology referral criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management. NICE guideline NG148. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: The volume state decides treatment: isotonic fluid for hypovolaemic hyponatraemia, never fluid restriction (European 2014).
